comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM disclose specific metrics related to their Asset & Wealth Management segments, but they measure different aspects of the business. GS focuses on the carrying value of specific consolidated investments classified as 'held for sale' within this segment, reporting a decline from $327 million to $517 million. In contrast, JPM reports the total scale of client assets under management for the same segment, showing significant growth from $5.0 trillion to $5.9 trillion. While both disclosures identify Asset & Wealth Management as a key reporting segment, the financial substance differs: GS highlights asset disposals/reclassifications within the segment, whereas JPM highlights the growth in aggregate client assets.
